VERDICT: CLEAN
BOUNDARY: The domain \(I\) may be any order-convex set, including empty, a singleton, unbounded intervals, or degenerate closed intervals. In all cases the theorem holds vacuously or trivially: for empty or singleton domains the strict monotonicity and continuity of the inverse follow from vacuous definitions or isolated-point continuity, and the proof’s existential steps remain logically valid under the assumption of non‑strict monotonicity. The reduction of the decreasing case to the increasing one via \(F = -f\) preserves order‑convexity of the image, and no boundary counterexample was found.
SOURCES: Every supplied cited item (L1–L6) was inspected. L1 (`thm-continuous-injection-on-an-interval-is-strictly-monotone`) exactly matches the needed hypothesis; L2 (`cor-continuous-image-of-an-interval-is-an-interval`, claim 1) guarantees order‑convexity of \(f[I]\); L3 (`lem-monotone-with-interval-image-is-continuous`) applies to the inverse with the required nondecreasing property and order‑convex image; L4 (`thm-algebra-of-continuous-functions` and `thm-composition-of-continuous-functions`) justifies continuity of \(-f\) and composition; L5 (`def-injection-surjection-bijection`) gives the bijection and two‑sided inverse; L6 (`def-monotone-function` and `def-interval`) correctly handles the monotonicity direction and order‑convexity under negation. All cited statements are properly aligned with the usage.
CHECKED: The title, the full public statement (five claims), every numbered proof step (1.1 – 7.1), and the Remarks were verified. The reasoning is logically sound; no missing hypothesis, circularity, or invalid inference was detected. Minor justificatory gaps (e.g., order‑convexity of \(-f[I]\)) are instantly closable by a competent reader and do not affect the overall correctness.
